subject: Request: exceptional onboarding credit + billing offset for CardioAI pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@cardioai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask — onboarding credit + billing structuring

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — the Redwood runtime looks like a strong fit for our clinical summarization pipeline. We are preparing a small, high-touch pilot (6 months) focused on cardiology transcription validation; expected consumption is ~75M tokens/month initially, ramping to ~180M.

Two asks from procurement/finance to move quickly:
- One-time onboarding credit to help cover engineering ramp & data ingestion (~$60k).
- Billing offset for the first 3 months (apply credit against invoices; CardioAI prefers NET30 invoicing rather than prepayment).

We are targeting an LOI within three weeks if we can align commercial and security terms; CardioAI is prepared to commit to a 36-month enterprise agreement if the pilot shows expected throughput.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide the onboarding credit and temporary billing offset while we complete procurement? If there are guardrails you need (usage floors, milestone checks), tell me and we can work them into the mutual action plan.

Appreciate it — Jordan

Jordan Miller
Head of Platform
CardioAI
jordan.miller@cardioai.com
+1 (415) 555-0134
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@cardioai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — onboarding credit + billing structuring

Jordan —

Really glad CardioAI is moving forward; the pilot profile and ramp look promising. I will circle internal stakeholders and escalate an exception memo for the requested $60k onboarding credit and the three-month billing offset.

Quick notes:
- We prefer structuring credits as invoice offsets rather than separate refunds.
- For billing terms, we can be flexible on NET30 for the pilot if procurement signs the standard MSA and we capture usage milestones.
- Need signoff from Finance (Marissa) for the credit and from Sales Ops (Ben) to operationalize billing changes.

Looping you out for now; Marissa/Ben — please see the message from CardioAI below. I drafted a short exception memo (attached as internal calc) and recommend approval with a 3-month offset and a milestone clause that gates the second month of offset on a usage check.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: FW: CardioAI pilot — internal exception memo (requesting CFO signoff)

Marissa / Ben —

FW: request from CardioAI. Below is a concise exception memo for Finance approval. I included an internal impact calc (attached) and a recommended fallback policy. Please review and sign off (or propose edits). We need a final answer to CardioAI by EOD tomorrow to keep the LOI cadence.

-- Exception memo (internal) --
Request: One-time onboarding credit of $60,000 plus a billing offset applied to the first three invoices (pilot only). Waive prepayment requirement for the pilot; accept NET30.
Rationale:
- Strategic, high-visibility pilot with a potential TOC → enterprise expansion (CardioAI indicates a 36-month commitment potential; forecasted ARR $2.4M).
- High usage density in initial months will create strong unit economics; the credit accelerates ingestion and shortens the evaluation cycle.
- CardioAI is in regulated healthcare; we will require SOC2 evidence and contractual data protections before live traffic.
Financial impact (summary):
- Upfront credit: $60,000 (applied as invoice offsets over first three invoices)
- Expected revenue from account (36 months): $2,400,000 (forecast)
- Payback window on credit (base case): ~4 months after pilot converts to committed tier (see attached calc)
Recommended guardrails:
1) Gate month-2 offset on meeting a minimum usage threshold (50M tokens/month).
2) If usage < threshold by end of month-2, credit drawdown limited to 50%.
3) SOC2 report and standard DPA signed prior to production.
4) Accounting to track credit as contra-revenue until conversion.

Attachments: cardioai_impact_calc.xlsx (internal model)

Ask: Marissa — CFO signoff required for credit > $50k and deviation from standard prepayment. Ben — please confirm whether Sales Ops can operationalize the 3-month invoice-offset approach.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: CardioAI pilot — internal exception memo (requesting CFO signoff)

Vanessa / Ben —

Thanks for the clear memo and the model — good work. I approve an exception with the following edits to reduce risk:

1) Reduce unconditional onboarding credit to $40,000; remaining $20,000 will be contingent and only drawn if CardioAI meets the month-2 usage threshold (>= 50M tokens).
2) Require SOC2 attestation (Type II) and execution of our standard DPA before we enable production traffic.
3) Billing offset: allow invoice offsets for months 1–3 but cap total offset applied in any month to 50% of that invoice to preserve cash flow.
4) Add a clawback clause in the SOW: if customer does not convert to signed committed tier within 120 days after pilot, remaining unearned credit becomes payable to Redwood.

Ben — please confirm Sales Ops can implement the offset/cap and track the clawback in the billing system. Once Ben confirms, I will sign (attaching signed approval).

Marissa Cole
VP Finance / CFO (acting) | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachment: cardioai_approval_signed.pdf
